scope: Generic educational descriptions only; vehicle-specific procedures and specifications must be sourced separately.
verification_policy: All records are needs_review. Source candidates are discovery starting points, not evidence that each claim has been verified. Do not promote to verified until a specific supporting document and relevant passage are recorded in entity_sources.

records.description: A replaceable filter element that removes airborne particles from intake air before it enters the engine.
records.main_function: Reduce dust and abrasive contaminants entering the intake and cylinders while allowing the required airflow.
records.installation_location: Usually inside an air-filter housing in the engine intake path; exact position varies by vehicle.
records.working_principle: Intake air passes through porous filter media. Particles are retained by the media while cleaned air continues toward the throttle body or compressor.
common_failures: Torn or incorrectly seated filter media
failure_symptoms: Possible reduced performance or increased fuel consumption when severely restricted
Dust traces downstream may indicate sealing or filter damage
testing_methods: Inspect media and sealing surfaces
Check the housing is correctly closed
If restriction is suspected, use the vehicle manufacturer's specified inspection or pressure-drop procedure
required_tools: Basic hand tools if housing access requires them

records.description: A filter in the engine lubrication circuit that removes contaminants suspended in circulating engine oil.
records.main_function: Limit abrasive particles and contaminants circulating through lubricated engine components.
records.installation_location: In the engine oil circuit; may be a spin-on canister or a replaceable cartridge inside a housing.
records.working_principle: Oil flows through filter media. Many designs include bypass and anti-drainback functions, but their presence and arrangement depend on the filter and engine design.
internal_components: End caps and center tube where applicable
failure_symptoms: Oil-pressure warning may occur in some fault conditions but is not proof of filter failure
Contaminated oil or abnormal service findings
testing_methods: Inspect for leaks and correct fitment
Verify part number and application
Follow manufacturer oil-pressure and filter inspection procedures

records.description: An electronically or hydraulically controlled metering device that delivers fuel into an intake port or directly into a combustion chamber, depending on injection architecture.
records.main_function: Meter and deliver fuel in a controlled quantity and spray pattern at the required time.
records.installation_location: Port injectors are mounted in the intake manifold or cylinder head near intake ports; direct injectors are installed in the cylinder head and enter the combustion chamber.
records.working_principle: An actuator opens a precision valve for a commanded interval. Fuel pressure, injector flow characteristics, temperature, fuel properties and control strategy affect delivered quantity.
internal_components: Inlet filter or screen where fitted
Solenoid or piezoelectric actuator depending on design
failure_symptoms: Fuel odor or leakage in relevant failure modes
testing_methods: Read DTCs and relevant live data
Perform electrical checks using the correct wiring diagram and specified method
Use approved balance, leak, or flow testing equipment appropriate to injector type
Observe high-pressure fuel safety procedures for GDI and diesel common-rail systems

records.description: A pump that moves fuel from the tank or a low-pressure supply stage toward the engine fuel system.
records.main_function: Provide the fuel flow and pressure required by the applicable fuel-delivery architecture.
records.installation_location: May be inside or near the fuel tank; high-pressure pumps in direct-injection systems are commonly engine-mounted. Layout varies by design.
records.working_principle: An electric or mechanically driven pumping element raises fuel pressure. Some systems use staged low- and high-pressure pumps with electronic control.
internal_components: Check or pressure-control components depending on design
common_failures: Restricted inlet strainer or fuel filter
testing_methods: Check applicable DTCs and commanded/actual pressure data
Verify power, ground and control using the correct wiring diagram
Measure pressure or flow only with equipment and procedures approved for that system
required_tools: Fuel-pressure test equipment rated for the system

records.description: An intake-air control assembly containing a throttle plate that regulates airflow in many spark-ignition engines.
records.main_function: Control intake airflow in response to driver demand and engine-management commands.
records.installation_location: Usually between the air-intake duct and intake manifold, though layouts vary.
records.working_principle: The throttle plate rotates to change the effective airflow area. Electronic throttle bodies use an electric motor and position feedback; older designs may use a cable.
internal_components: Return spring and gears where fitted
testing_methods: Inspect intake ducting and throttle plate according to service procedure
Compare commanded and actual throttle position with scan data
Perform electrical checks using vehicle-specific specifications
Use manufacturer-prescribed relearn procedures when required
required_tools: Scan tool with suitable data and service functions
Approved cleaning materials if cleaning is permitted

records.description: An insulated electrode assembly that creates an electrical spark inside a spark-ignition engine combustion chamber.
records.main_function: Initiate combustion by producing a spark across the electrode gap at the commanded ignition timing.
records.installation_location: Threaded into the cylinder head with the electrodes exposed to the combustion chamber.
records.working_principle: The ignition system raises voltage sufficiently to ionize the gap and create a spark. Required plug design and gap depend on engine specification.
testing_methods: Inspect plug condition and deposits using service guidance
Check correct part number and specified gap where adjustable
Use appropriate ignition diagnosis; do not infer coil failure from plug appearance alone
required_tools: Feeler gauge only where the design permits gap measurement or adjustment

records.description: An inductive ignition component that stores energy in a magnetic field and generates the high voltage needed to fire a spark plug.
records.main_function: Transform the ignition system's low-voltage supply into a high-voltage output for spark generation.
records.installation_location: May be mounted remotely, in a coil pack, or directly above an individual spark plug.
records.working_principle: Current through the primary winding builds a magnetic field. When primary current is switched off by the ignition driver, the collapsing field induces high voltage in the secondary winding.
testing_methods: Use scan data and misfire counters where available
Inspect coil, boot and plug well
Perform approved primary/secondary circuit tests; resistance alone may not identify all modern coil faults
Use an oscilloscope or approved tester where appropriate
required_tools: Automotive oscilloscope or ignition tester where appropriate

records.description: A sensor that measures the mass flow rate of air entering an engine on systems that use MAF-based load calculation.
records.main_function: Provide the engine controller with an air-mass measurement used for fuel and torque management.
records.installation_location: Typically installed in the intake duct between the air filter and throttle body or turbocharger, depending on layout.
records.working_principle: Common hot-film or hot-wire designs measure the electrical energy needed to maintain a sensing element at a controlled temperature as intake air flows past it.
common_failures: Power, ground or signal circuit fault
Incorrect sensor installation or airflow disturbance
testing_methods: Check DTCs, freeze-frame and fuel trims
Inspect air filter, ducting and clamps for leaks
Compare MAF data with engine speed/load and manufacturer reference information
Check supply, ground and signal according to wiring diagram
required_tools: Smoke tester for intake leaks where appropriate

records.description: A pressure sensor that measures absolute pressure in the intake manifold or a connected pressure passage.
records.main_function: Supply manifold-pressure information for engine load estimation and control strategies.
records.installation_location: Mounted on the intake manifold or connected by a pressure passage or hose, depending on design.
records.working_principle: A pressure-sensitive element changes an electrical characteristic; integrated electronics condition the signal for the engine controller.
common_failures: Reference, ground or signal wiring fault
Leak or damaged pressure hose where fitted
testing_methods: Compare key-on/engine-off pressure data with local atmospheric pressure using appropriate context
Check running data against manufacturer specifications
Inspect pressure port or hose
Test reference, ground and signal using the correct wiring diagram
required_tools: Hand vacuum/pressure source only if approved for the sensor

records.description: A sensor that detects crankshaft position and rotational speed from a trigger wheel or target feature.
records.main_function: Provide crank angle and engine-speed information required for ignition, injection and engine synchronization.
records.installation_location: Usually positioned near the crankshaft reluctor or trigger wheel, often at the block, bellhousing or front cover.
records.working_principle: May use an inductive variable-reluctance element or a Hall-effect/magnetoresistive design. Signal form and biasing depend on sensor type and ECU input circuit.
internal_components: Magnetic core or semiconductor element depending on design
testing_methods: Check scan-tool engine-speed and synchronization data while cranking
Inspect sensor mounting, target wheel and harness
Identify sensor type before electrical testing
Capture waveform using an oscilloscope and compare with vehicle-specific reference

records.description: A sensor that reports camshaft phase or position so the engine controller can determine cylinder phase and manage synchronization and variable valve timing.
records.main_function: Support engine synchronization, sequential injection and camshaft control strategies.
records.installation_location: Mounted near a camshaft target, cylinder head or timing cover depending on engine design.
records.working_principle: Common designs use Hall-effect or magnetoresistive sensing; some older designs use inductive technology. The ECU interprets the signal relative to crankshaft position.
common_failures: Timing-chain/belt or cam-phaser problem causing correlation error
testing_methods: Review cam/crank synchronization data
Inspect connector and mechanical timing evidence
Capture waveform and compare cam-to-crank correlation with manufacturer reference
Do not replace the sensor solely because a correlation code is present

records.description: A temperature sensor used by the engine controller or other modules to monitor coolant temperature.
records.main_function: Provide temperature information for cold-start fueling, fan strategy, thermal protection and instrument display, depending on system architecture.
records.installation_location: Typically installed in a coolant passage, cylinder head, thermostat housing or coolant outlet.
records.working_principle: Many automotive coolant sensors use an NTC thermistor whose resistance decreases as temperature rises; exact calibration and circuit design are application-specific.
testing_methods: Compare cold-soak scan data with ambient conditions
Monitor warm-up trend for plausibility
Test resistance or signal only against the correct sensor specification
Inspect connector and coolant leakage

records.description: A temperature-responsive valve that regulates coolant flow between engine and radiator circuits to help manage engine operating temperature.
records.main_function: Control coolant circulation through the radiator according to thermal conditions.
records.installation_location: Usually located in a housing at an engine coolant outlet or within an integrated coolant module.
records.working_principle: A conventional wax-element thermostat expands with temperature and moves a valve. Electronically controlled or mapped thermostats may use an additional heater or actuator.
common_failures: Electrical control fault on mapped designs
failure_symptoms: Slow warm-up or low operating temperature
Overheating if coolant flow is restricted
testing_methods: Assess warm-up behavior using scan data
Check radiator hose temperature patterns only as a supporting observation
Follow manufacturer procedure for removal and bench testing where specified
Never open a hot pressurized cooling system

records.description: A heat exchanger that transfers heat from engine coolant to ambient air in liquid-cooled vehicles.
records.main_function: Reject heat from coolant to help maintain the engine within its designed thermal operating range.
records.installation_location: Usually mounted at the front of the vehicle behind the grille, though packaging varies.
records.working_principle: Hot coolant flows through tubes and fins. Airflow across the finned core removes heat; airflow may be provided by vehicle motion and cooling fans.
testing_methods: Inspect coolant level only when safe and cold
Pressure-test using the specified procedure and cap rating
Inspect airflow path and fan operation
Use approved methods to assess restriction; do not diagnose by touch alone

source_candidates.title: Thermal management and heat exchanger information

records.description: A pump that circulates coolant through the engine and cooling circuit in many liquid-cooled vehicles.
records.main_function: Maintain coolant circulation through the engine, radiator and associated heat exchangers as designed.
records.installation_location: May be driven by the timing belt, accessory belt, an electric motor or integrated thermal-management module.
records.working_principle: An impeller moves coolant through the circuit. Drive method and speed control vary between mechanical and electric designs.
internal_components: Shaft and bearing in mechanical designs
Electric motor and control electronics on electric designs
failure_symptoms: Bearing noise on some mechanical designs
Poor circulation or related fault codes
testing_methods: Inspect for leakage and drive condition
Check commanded and actual operation on electric pumps where scan data is available
Use manufacturer procedure to assess circulation and pump performance
Never remove a hot pressurized cap
